chunks: With this chain of narration, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father and Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Layth al-Murādī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man may have boils and sores, so that his skin and his clothes are filled with blood and pus. He said: “He prays in his clothes, and he does not wash them, and there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.الدَّمَامِيلُ: boils or inflamed swellings on the body
key_terms.وَ لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: and there is no liability or blame upon him
key_terms.وَ لَا يَغْسِلُهَا: and he does not wash them

ai.seo_question: Can a person pray in clothes stained with blood and pus from boils or sores?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person afflicted with boils and sores whose body and clothing are covered with blood and pus. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that such a person may perform salat (prayer) in those clothes without washing them, and no blame is upon him, indicating a concession in cases of ongoing hardship.
